newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wages dent hopes of rate cut bulls.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wages dent hopes of rate cut bulls.

text.p: Prospects for a fourth Australian rate cut were dented on Thursday by news that wages growth was running at a quicker pace than most had expected.
The news gave the Australian dollar some respite after being under pressure since the last cut in December, but it deflated bonds, which have been bullish on the prospects of a cut.

"Considering that they've already eased rates 150 basis points since July, the Reserve Bank will be looking for that to kick into the economy," Colonial State Bank chief economist Hans Kunnen said. "Maybe we have seen the bottom of interest rates."
Average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) rose 1.2 percent in the three months to November, at the top end of expectations which had centred on a 0.9 percent rise.

In annual terms, wages growth was at 3.9 percent, again at the top end of expectations. It also was above the annual rate in August of 3.8 percent, the first time since August 1995 that the annual pace of wages growth has risen.

While the level of wages growth at around 4.0 percent remained consistent with the Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA) underlying inflation objective, there were some signs that wages growth may have troughed.
